title: fix: publish SDK through npm OIDC
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes SDK publishing authentication by using GitHub OIDC and Node 24, following the existing CLI publisher.
- Triggers the SDK publisher when the release workflow changes so the unpublished `5.1.0-alpha.7` can be recovered on merge.
- Preserves the `alpha` dist-tag and already-published version check.
- Validated with actionlint, SDK build, 73 tests, and npm pack dry run. Biome does not process this YAML file.
- Requires npm Trusted Publishing for `@pollinations/sdk`: repository `pollinations/pollinations`, workflow `release-publish-npm-packages.yml`, permission to run `npm publish`. Package configuration and live publication are pending.

Addresses #14514

gist.headline: The SDK gets a passport
gist.blurb: The SDK release worker now uses GitHub OIDC to prove it belongs at npm. Alpha packages can resume their small but important journey from hive to registry.
gist.summary: Updated the SDK npm publishing workflow to use GitHub OIDC with Node 24, preserve the alpha dist-tag and published-version check, and rerun publishing when the release workflow changes so @pollinations/sdk 5.1.0-alpha.7 can be recovered.
gist.impact: Once npm Trusted Publishing is configured for @pollinations/sdk, SDK alpha releases can publish through the same OIDC-based path as the CLI without maintaining a separate npm authentication secret.
gist.visual_concept: Polli wears a tiny passport-holder scarf and presents an official OIDC badge at a cozy npm package-post office, while a CRT monitor robot stamps an @pollinations/sdk alpha parcel; code-plants and a lime-green release conveyor represent the automated publishing path.
